Deep learning-based image classification systems individually developed by various convolutional neural architecture variants are computationally expensive. Although, leveraging an existing trained neural network and creating an ensemble of predictions by multiple slightly varied versions of the neural architecture is proven to substantially enhance accuracy. In analogy to traditional machine learning approaches, this strategy constructs an ensemble analogous to techniques like bagging and boosting, but lacks research into various subsetting and enhancement methodologies commonly employed in ensemble learning. In an effort to fill this knowledge gap, our research investigates various ensemble learning techniques including but not limited to passive aggregation, weighting, boosting, and batching methods applied to the convolutional neural architecture ensemble. In addition, we explore multiple feature selection algorithms applicable to learning an subset of ensembles to achieve optimal accuracy with minimal number of neural network evaluations. Our findings demonstrate that employing boosting and feature selection techniques, specifically stochastic gradient boosting and random subsetting, along with a newly proposed measure called covariance of predictions can substantially enhance accuracy of convolutional neural architecture ensemble with minimal overhead compared to standard passive aggregation of ensembles. Our code is publicly accessible on GitHub at https://github.com/wengwengxD/CNES.

The study analyzes the W and Z boson structure functions at very high energies up to $10^9$ Gluon Per Nucleon using the modern W/Z PDF formalism. Based on universal logarithmic and non-linear Bodwin-Soper-Vermen (BSV) evolution corrections, this approach treats W/Z quarks and gluons as reflecting the underlying proton structure. Building on recent W/Z LHE matching BSM effective field theory (EFT) operators, it incorporates W/Z production in direct gamma-gluon interactions and in nonlinear proton proton scattering and proton splitting phenomena. 

Consistent theoretical derivations and calculations show that after W/Z and gluon BSV evolution, modified BSV corrections significantly enhance the energy of the W and Z quarks and gluons, especially at very high energies beyond traditional BSV nonlinear thresholds. Modified BSV corrections are found to be negligible around a meson threshold but exhibit a steep rise beyond a wimpy threshold, reflecting a nonlinear BSV threshold surge in direct gamma-gluon interactions and in W/Z BSV BSM effective field theory (EFT) proton proton scattering and proton splitting threshold enhancements. 

Universal BSV nonlinear threshold enhancements are found to drive a nonlinear unification of the W and Z electromagnetic weak isospin forces at extremely high energies beyond traditional BSV evolution scales, giving rise to a nonlinear W/Z electromagnetic weak symmetry. The proof by Godel established that within any sufficiently complex and consistent formal system, there exists at least one undecidable sentence. Building on this finding, Rosper demonstrated a stronger claim: within any sufficiently complex and consistent formal system, there are infinitely many undecidable sentences. Although multiple proofs of the Rosper theorem have since been developed, most rely directly or indirectly on the Godel theorem. This paper presents a new, direct proof of the undelikability of certain sentences within any consistent formal system of integer arithmetic, without necessitating the use of the Godel numbering approach or a related lemma from Godel's original proof.

Fractional-order linear systems are analyzed for their invariant subspaces, with a focus on characterizing them and providing a method to decompose the system's state space. A specific condition is identified for an invariant subspace to apply to fractional order systems, leading to a complete description of all invariant subspaces. The discussion extends to invariant subspaces for specific classes of system matrices, with a particular emphasis on those that are regular and pole-free at the point $s=0$.

We establish unique continuation properties and derive stability estimates for inverse problems within a subset of a domain for parabolic partial differential equations, using an source term that varies over time and is measurable, as well as observation data over a sub-region and the same time period. A novel approach is employed, building on a recent method developed for elliptic equations, by deriving an inequality ensuring stability of inverse problems for parabolic equations with an initial condition set zero, mirning a uniqueness result proved earlier.

We explore the concept of dark parity within a minimal dark sector incorporating a singlet scalar and a singlet fermion, and examine its viability through both minimal and maximal implementations of spontaneous dark parity violation. In the context of the seesaw mechanism, we assess the implications of radiative corrections on fermion masses and examine the stability of the vacuum as well as the scale at which dark parity loses its relevance.
